summary.intent: Conduct a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch and implement any high-confidence vulnerabilities found.
summary.outcome: Identified a HIGH severity crypto verification bypass (missing pubKey-to-ipnsName binding) and implemented the fix in both sdk-core and the web app.

repo: IPNS resolution has a zero-knowledge trust model — clients sign locally, never send private keys to server; server only relays to DHT
The web app's ipns.service.ts is a thin wrapper: local crypto via @cipherbox/core, Ed25519 via @cipherbox/crypto, transport via generated API client
deriveIpnsName() is exported from @cipherbox/crypto and can derive the IPNS name from a raw Ed25519 public key
signatureVerified is returned as an informational boolean from resolveIpnsRecord — callers are not required to enforce it
The TEE republish service enrolls IPNS records for background republishing to the DHT

code.finding: Added pubKey-to-ipnsName binding check: after signature verification, decode returned pubKey, derive expected IPNS name via deriveIpnsName(), throw if it doesn't match the requested ipnsName
Same pubKey-to-ipnsName binding check added here — both SDK and web service had the same gap

workflow: Security review used a 3-phase approach: identification subagent → parallel false-positive filter subagents → confidence threshold filtering (>8)
The diff was too large (109KB) for inline context and was saved to a persisted tool-results file

friction: Full diff was 109KB and couldn't be inlined — required reading from a persisted file path
deriveIpnsName availability had to be verified via grep before applying fix
open_items: Callers of resolveIpnsRecord do not enforce signatureVerified===true — intentionally deferred, but means server can bypass signature verification by omitting signature fields
The backend's ipns.service.ts stores raw signed_record bytes in DB — no review of whether those bytes are validated before being returned to clients on cached resolves
